napoleon-crossing-the-alps.text: Before you rides Napoleon, painted by David in 1801.
Notice his calm face on a wild, rearing horse.
In truth, he crossed on a mule.

wanderer-above-the-sea-of-fog.text: Before you stands a lone traveller above a sea of fog, painted by Friedrich around 1818.
Notice how we share his view.

the-fifer.text: Before you stands a young army musician, painted by Manet in 1866.
Notice the plain grey background: so daring, the Paris Salon rejected it.

the-blue-boy.text: Before you stands Gainsborough's Blue Boy, painted around 1770.
Notice the shimmering blue silk, a costume already old-fashioned in his day.

louis-xiv.text: Before you stands King Louis the Fourteenth, painted by Rigaud in 1701.
It was meant as a gift for Spain, but the king kept it.

napoleon-in-his-study.text: Before you, Napoleon stands in his study, painted by David in 1812.
Notice the clock: past four in the morning.

colonel-heathcote.text: Before you stands Colonel Charles Heathcote, painted by Joseph Wright of Derby around 1771.
Notice how he points out across the landscape.

saint-jerome.text: Before you sits Saint Jerome, painted by Jusepe de Ribera around 1640.
Notice the skull, a quiet reminder that life is short.

caillebotte-man.text: Before you sits a gentleman, painted by Gustave Caillebotte in 1880.
Notice how relaxed he is, leaning back by the window.

lotto-man.text: Before you, a gentleman stretches out his hand, painted by Lorenzo Lotto around 1534.
Notice the dramatic gesture, as if he is speaking to us.

saint-peter-repentant.text: Before you sits Saint Peter, painted by Georges de La Tour in 1645.
Notice the rooster: it crowed after Peter denied knowing Jesus.

the-tired-gleaner.text: Before you, a tired gleaner stretches at sunset, painted by Jules Breton in 1880.
Notice her arm raised to her head after a long day.

charles-ii.text: Before you stands the young Charles the Second, painted by Philippe de Champaigne in 1653.
At the time, he was a king in exile.

saint-peter-of-alcantara.text: Before you stands Saint Peter of Alcántara, carved and painted in wood by Pedro de Mena.
Notice the book held in his hands.

standing-apostle.text: Before you stands an apostle, perhaps Saint Paul, carved around 1430.
Notice the heavy folds of his robe.

woman-as-diana.text: Before you sits a lady dressed as Diana, goddess of the hunt, painted by Jean-Marc Nattier in 1752.
Notice the bow and the leopard skin.

mary-magdalen-vouet.text: Before you, Mary Magdalen looks up to heaven, painted by Simon Vouet around 1630.
Notice her hand pressed to her heart.

arnolfini-portrait.text: Before you stand a merchant and his wife, painted by Jan van Eyck in 1434.
Notice how their hands meet between them.

the-ambassadors.text: Before you stand two French ambassadors, painted by Hans Holbein in 1533.
Notice the globes and instruments between them.

romeo-and-juliet.text: Before you, Romeo and Juliet say goodbye at dawn, painted by Ford Madox Brown.
Notice how tightly they hold each other.

mr-and-mrs-andrews.text: Before you are Mr and Mrs Andrews on their estate, painted by Thomas Gainsborough around 1750.
Notice how relaxed he looks beside her bench.

the-jewish-bride.text: Before you is Rembrandt's Jewish Bride, painted in the late 1660s.
Notice the groom's gentle hand resting near the bride's heart.

henry-viii.text: Before you stands King Henry the Eighth, after a portrait by Hans Holbein.
Notice his wide stance and broad shoulders: pure royal power.

lansdowne-washington.text: Before you stands George Washington, painted by Gilbert Stuart in 1796.
Notice his outstretched arm, as if he is giving a speech.

laughing-cavalier.text: Before you is Frans Hals's Laughing Cavalier, painted in 1624.
Notice his hand on his hip and his proud, confident smile.

madame-x.text: Before you stands Madame X, painted by John Singer Sargent in 1884.
Notice how she turns her head proudly to the side.

little-dancer.text: Before you stands Degas's Little Dancer, modelled around 1880.
Notice her hands held behind her back and her chin held high.

mona-lisa.text: Before you sits the Mona Lisa, painted by Leonardo da Vinci.
Notice her folded hands and that famous, mysterious smile.

innocent-x.text: Before you sits Pope Innocent the Tenth, painted by Velázquez in 1650.
Notice his sharp, watchful eyes and the paper in his hand.
